title: Exploring the open-aperture nonlinear optical and organic luminescent properties of a novel triazolium glutarate (TAG) single crystal
content: Centrosymmetric nonlinear optical (NLO) crystals were effectively grown at room temperature using the slow-evaporation solution technique. The crystal structure and lattice parameters of the grown crystal were determined by single-crystal X-ray diffraction (SXRD), and the TAG crystal was found to be monoclinic with the space group P21/c. The active functional groups were investigated by FTIR spectroscopic analysis. The optical properties were observed at 3.3 eV with a cutoff wavelength of 413 nm, and thermal studies revealed that the grown crystal is stable up to 192 °C. Dielectric studies of the TAG crystal were conducted at room temperature in a frequency range of 100 Hz to 6 MHz. Steady-state photo luminescence spectra were recorded at an excitation wavelength of 300 nm and its violet emission at 409 nm; the weighted-average lifetime τavg is calculated to be 0.95 µs. A Nd:YAG laser operated at 532 nm was used to analyze the third-order nonlinear optical behaviour by employing the open-aperture Z-scan technique with varying intensities (50–200 µJ). The TAG crystal exhibited reverse saturable absorption and a rapid decrease in the optical limiting threshold with an increase in the nonlinear absorption coefficient. Quantum-chemical calculations were performed using the DFT method at the UB3LYP/6-311G(d,p) level to evaluate the HOMO–LUMO energy gap, IR spectra, NBOs and nonlinear properties (dipole moment, polarizability, and hyperpolarizability). The calculated HOMO–LUMO energy gap is 2.98 eV. Based on the observed results, the TAG crystal shows suitability for OLEDs, photonic limiters and photonic switching applications.
